turns.speaker: user

endings.moshi: Then keep her in for a few weeks first so she learns it's home. Start with short supervised trips before dinner, so she comes back hungry.

endings.user: Indoors. I'd worry about the road.
endings.moshi: That's completely okay. A window perch, a cat tree and some daily play will keep her happy inside.

endings.moshi: They often do, so lifetime makes sense. Check the yearly limit per condition, that's the bit that really matters.

endings.moshi: That can work if you're disciplined. Set up a separate savings pot so it's not touched for anything else.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How often should I take my dog to the vet?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: For a healthy adult dog, a checkup once a year is standard. Puppies and older dogs need visits more often.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She's about nine now. Is that considered old?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: For many breeds, yes, that's senior. Twice a year checkups are a good idea from here on.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She's been sleeping a lot more lately / is that something to worry about?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Some extra sleep is normal with age. But if she's also eating less or seems stiff, mention it to the vet.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She does seem slow on the stairs.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That could be joint pain, which is very common and treatable. Ask the vet about it at her next visit.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My daughter wants a hamster for her birthday. Are they good first pets?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: They can be, but they're awake mostly at night and can nip if handled roughly. How old is she?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She's turning eight.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a fine age with some supervision. A big cage, a wheel and a deep layer of bedding are the essentials.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Would a guinea pig be better? I've heard / they're friendlier.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Guinea pigs are usually calmer and awake during the day, so they're great with kids. But they're happier in pairs.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Two of them? That's double the cleaning.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: True, but one cage and they keep each other company. It's honestly not much more work.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can dogs eat grapes? Mine just grabbed one off the floor.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Grapes can be toxic to dogs, even in small amounts. Please call your vet or a pet poison line right away.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It was just one grape. He's a big dog.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Even so, it's best to call. The reaction varies a lot between dogs, and they can tell you what to watch for.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'll call them now. What else should I keep away from him?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Chocolate, raisins, onions, garlic and anything with xylitol, which is a sweetener in some gum and peanut butter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Wow, I had no idea about the / the peanut butter one.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Most peanut butter is fine, just check the label for xylitol before sharing.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I adopted a cat last week and she's hiding under the bed all day.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's really normal for a new cat. Give her a quiet room with food, water and a litter box nearby.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I try to pull her out so she gets used to me?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Better not. Let her come out on her own. Sit nearby and read or talk softly so she learns you're safe.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How long does it usually take?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Anywhere from a few days to a few weeks. Treats and a feather toy can speed things up.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll pick up a feather toy tomorrow / and maybe some of those lickable treats.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Great idea. Cats tend to love those, and it's a nice way to build trust.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Why does my dog eat grass and then throw up? Is he sick?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lots of dogs eat grass, and most of the time it's harmless. Some just like the taste, others do it when their tummy feels a bit off.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He does it every single walk.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If he's otherwise eating, playing and pooping normally, it's usually nothing to worry about.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He seems totally fine. / Annoyingly fine, actually.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then it's probably habit. Just keep him off grass that might be sprayed with weedkiller.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And when should I worry?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If he's vomiting a lot, not eating, seems tired or the sick has blood in it, call your vet.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My cat yowls at four in the morning. Every morning. I'm losing my mind.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That sounds rough. Cats are naturally most active around dawn, and she's probably learned that yowling gets you up.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I do get up and feed her, yeah.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's the reward she's after. Try an automatic feeder that opens at dawn, so the food doesn't come from you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Smart. What else?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Play with her hard in the evening, like ten or fifteen minutes with a wand toy, then give her dinner. Tired, full cats sleep longer.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And if she still screams?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ignore it completely, no talking, no getting up. It usually gets worse for a few nights before it stops, so hang in there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We just got a border collie. How much exercise does she actually need?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A lot. Most collies want a couple of hours of activity a day, and just as importantly, things for their brain to do.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Two hours? We both work.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It doesn't all have to be walking. Training games, sniffing hunts and puzzle toys tire them out surprisingly well.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What happens if she doesn't get enough?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Bored collies tend to invent their own jobs, like herding the kids, chewing furniture, or barking at everything.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She already herds my son. / He thinks it's hilarious.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's sweet now, but nipping at heels can grow into a habit. Give her a proper outlet, like fetch or a beginner agility class.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm bringing home a second cat next week. How do I introduce them without a war?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Go slowly. Keep the new cat in a separate room for the first few days with her own food, water and litter tray.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: They can't see each other at all?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not yet. Let them get used to each other's smell first. Swap their bedding or rub a cloth on one and leave it near the other.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And then?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Feed them on either side of a closed door, then a door open a crack, then a baby gate. Move on only when both are eating calmly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How long does all this take?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Anything from a week to a month. Hissing at first is normal, so don't panic if it's not instant friendship.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm terrified of cutting my dog's nails. I'm scared I'll hit the quick.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Totally understandable. Take tiny slices off the tip rather than one big cut, and stop when you see a darker dot in the middle.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: His nails are black. I can't see anything.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Black nails are harder. Just trim a thin sliver at a time and look at the cut surface, when it starts looking moist or chalky in the centre, stop.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And if I make it bleed?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Press some styptic powder or even cornflour onto the tip for a minute. It looks worse than it is.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe I'll / just pay the vet nurse to do it.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's fine too. Some people walk their dogs on pavements more, which wears the nails down naturally between trims.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My tortoise has gone very sleepy. Is she trying to hibernate?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Possibly, if the weather's cooling down. What kind of tortoise is she?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A Hermann's, I think. She's about ten.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hermann's do hibernate. But before letting her, it's important she's healthy and has had a vet check this autumn.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Why a vet check?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A tortoise that's underweight or ill can struggle to survive the winter. The vet will weigh her and check she's ready.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And then she just sleeps in a box?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Somewhere with a steady temperature, just above freezing, often in a fridge set up for it. Weigh her every couple of weeks to make sure she isn't losing too much.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you teach an old dog new tricks? Mine's eleven and he's never learned to give a paw.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Absolutely. Older dogs learn just fine, sometimes better, since they're calmer.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do I start?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hold a treat in your closed hand near his paw. The moment he lifts his paw to touch it, say yes and give him the treat.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What if he just sniffs it?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's normal. Wait. He'll try different things, and as soon as the paw lifts even a little, reward it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He's got a bad hip though.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then make sure he's comfy lying down, and keep sessions short, two or three minutes. Maybe teach him to touch your hand with his nose instead, it's gentler.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I just found a flea on my cat. Do I need to panic?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: No panic needed, but it's worth acting now. Where there's one flea there are usually more.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Gross. What do I do?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Get a vet recommended spot on treatment for cats. Never use a dog one, some of them are really toxic to cats.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh wow, I didn't know that.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's an important one. Treat every pet in the house, not just her.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the house itself? / Do I have to burn the sofa?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: No burning required. Vacuum everything thoroughly for a few weeks, wash her bedding hot, and empty the vacuum bag outside each time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My puppy bites my hands constantly. Her teeth are like needles.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Puppy teeth are vicious. Biting is normal at that age, she's exploring and teething, but you can teach her to be gentle.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How? She thinks it's a game.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: When she bites, stop playing immediately and go still. Then offer a toy she's allowed to chew instead.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And if she goes for my ankles?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Same thing. Freeze, be boring, then redirect to a tug toy. Running away makes it more exciting.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My kids keep squealing and running.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Teach them to be trees, stand still with arms folded. It's hard for kids, but it works fast if everyone does it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My budgie used to sing all day, and now he's really quiet. Should I worry?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's worth keeping an eye on. Has anything changed lately, like the cage spot, a new pet, or less daylight?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We moved his cage into the bedroom because of the cat.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That might be it. Budgies like being near the action and they get lonely easily.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is he eating okay?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's the key question. If he's eating, preening and his droppings look normal, it's probably mood. If he's fluffed up and sleepy, see an avian vet.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He's eating. He just / sits there looking sad.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Try moving him to a busy room that's safe from the cat, and talk to him through the day. Some people get a second budgie for company.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It's scorching today. Is it safe to walk my dog at lunchtime?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Probably not on pavement. Try the back of your hand on the ground for seven seconds, if it's too hot for you, it's too hot for his paws.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Seven seconds is a long time on that tarmac.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly. Walk early in the morning or late in the evening instead, and stick to grass and shade.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He'll go mad if he doesn't go out.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A short sniff around the garden and some indoor games will do for today. Frozen treats in a mat are great on hot days.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What signs would mean he's overheating?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Heavy panting, drooling a lot, being wobbly or very sleepy. If that happens, cool him with lukewarm water and call a vet.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My cat has started weeing on the bath mat instead of in her tray.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's frustrating. The first step is a vet visit, because urinary problems are a really common cause.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She seems healthy otherwise.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Cats hide pain well, so it's still worth ruling out. If she's fine, then it's usually something about the tray.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I did change the litter brand last week. / Because it was on offer.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That could be it. Cats can be really fussy about texture and smell. Go back to the old one and see if she returns.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And should I clean the bath mat with bleach?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Use an enzyme cleaner instead. Bleach can smell like urine to cats and might draw her back to the same spot.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We have a baby due in two months and a very spoiled dog. How do we prepare him?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good thinking to start now. Begin making small changes, like where he sleeps or which rooms he's allowed in, before the baby arrives.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He sleeps on our bed.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If that'll change, change it now, so he doesn't connect losing his spot with the baby.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's a good point.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You can also play recordings of baby crying at a low volume while giving him treats, so the sound becomes normal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And when we bring her home?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Let him sniff a blanket she's used first. Then let him meet her calmly with you holding her, and never leave them alone together.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do I pick a good vet? We've just moved here.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ask neighbours with pets and check local reviews. Then ring a couple of practices and see how they treat you on the phone.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What should I ask them?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ask about out of hours emergencies, whether they have a vet that likes cats or exotics if you need that, and how easy appointments are to get.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've got a rabbit and a dog.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then check they're comfortable with rabbits, not every vet is. Some practices have a special interest in them.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I register now even if no one's sick?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, do it now. It's much less stressful than trying to find one in an emergency at midnight.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My dog's breath could strip paint. What can I do?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Bad breath is often a sign of plaque or gum problems. A vet check is a good first step to look at his teeth.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I just brush them?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, brushing is the gold standard. Use a dog toothpaste, never human, and a soft brush or a finger brush.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He'd bite the brush in half.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Start small. Let him lick the toothpaste off your finger for a few days, then rub his gums gently, and build up from there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And dental chews?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: They help a bit, but they're not a replacement for brushing. Pick ones approved for dental health and count them as part of his food.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We had to say goodbye to our old dog yesterday. The house feels so empty.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: I'm really sorry. That first stretch after losing a dog is so hard, especially with all the little routines that are suddenly gone.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I keep reaching for the lead at seven.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's completely normal. Grief often shows up in those habits. It might help to still go for a short walk at that time, just for you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My son keeps asking if we'll get another one.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Kids often process grief that way. It's okay to say we'll think about it when we're ready.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I feel guilty even thinking about another dog. / It feels like replacing him.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lots of people feel that. A new dog wouldn't replace him, it'd be its own relationship. There's no right timing, only what feels right for your family.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I bring my dog to a cafe? I've never tried it.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lots of cafes welcome dogs, just check first. Go at a quieter time for your first visit so it's not overwhelming.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He's quite excitable around food.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then walk him well beforehand, so he's tired. Bring a mat and a long lasting chew so he has a job to do under the table.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What if he barks?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Calmly take him outside for a minute, then try again. If he can't settle, keep the visit short and try again another day.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And a water bowl?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Many places put one out, but a collapsible bowl in your bag is handy. Short positive visits will teach him cafes are boring, which is the goal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My daughter is allergic to cats and dogs but desperate for a pet. Are hypoallergenic dogs a real thing?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sort of. No dog is completely allergy free, but some breeds that shed less, like poodles, can cause fewer symptoms for some people.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So it's a gamble.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A bit. The best test is to spend time with that specific dog several times before committing.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And other pets?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Fish and reptiles are good options, since they don't have fur. Some kids with allergies do fine with certain birds too, though that varies.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She'd love a gecko, actually.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Leopard geckos are a popular first reptile, calm and easy to handle. They need a heated tank and a bit of research, but they're low allergy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My cat is a bit of a round boy. The vet said lose a kilo. How?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Slowly is the key, cats shouldn't lose weight too fast. Ask the vet for his exact daily food amount and weigh it out with kitchen scales.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He screams if his bowl's empty.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Split the daily amount into four or five small meals. More frequent meals feel like more food.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And treats? / He gets a few. Okay, a lot.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Take treats out of his daily allowance, or swap to tiny bits of cooked chicken.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He also doesn't really move much.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Get him chasing a feather wand for a few minutes twice a day. Even lazy cats will hunt something if it's interesting.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We adopted a rescue dog and she's terrified of my husband. Just him.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's actually common. Some rescue dogs had bad experiences with men, or just weren't around many when they were young.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He's heartbroken, he's the dog person in the family.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ask him to ignore her for a while, no eye contact, no reaching for her. Let her come to him.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's going to be hard for him.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's the fastest way though. He can sit on the floor and toss her really tasty treats without looking at her.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should he feed her meals too?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, that's a great idea. If he's the one who brings dinner and walks, she'll learn that good things come from him.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've moved house. Do I need to update my dog's microchip?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, you do. The chip only stores a number, and the database links it to your address and phone, so those need to be current.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do I do it?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Find which database the chip is registered with, usually on the paperwork from the breeder or rescue. Then log in or call to update.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've lost all the paperwork. / Of course.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: No problem. Ask your vet to scan him. They'll get the chip number, and you can look up which database it's on.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is there a fee?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Some databases charge a small fee for changes, some are free. Either way, it's much cheaper than losing him.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm getting a leopard gecko. What temperature does the tank need to be?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: They need a warm side and a cool side, so they can move between them. The warm spot should be around thirty degrees.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Celsius?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, Celsius. The cool end can be a lot lower, more like room temperature.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do I heat it?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Most people use a heat mat under one end controlled by a thermostat, or an overhead heat lamp. The thermostat is the important bit, so it doesn't overheat.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And a light at night?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: No, they need darkness at night to keep a healthy rhythm. Just keep the room from getting too cold.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My dog ignores me completely at the park. He comes back when he feels like it.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's frustrating and can be dangerous. Recall is all about making coming back the best thing ever.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I give him treats.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Use the really good stuff for recall only, like chicken or cheese, not his normal biscuits.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay. And when he ignores me?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Don't keep repeating his name. Practise in the garden first, then on a long training lead at the park, so he can't practise ignoring you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A long lead? Like a really long one?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Five or ten metres. It gives him freedom while you can still reel him in.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That sounds like a tangle waiting to happen.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It can be, so wear gloves and keep it short in busy areas. It's worth it, recall can save his life one day.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My neighbour is feeding my cats for a week. What should I write down for her?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Keep it simple. How much food, what time, and where the food and bowls are.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She's never had cats.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then add the basics, like how to scoop the litter, where the bags go, and to check they have fresh water.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: One of them is on tablets.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Write exactly how and when to give them, and maybe show her once before you go. Leave the pill packet out with the doses.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And emergencies?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Put your vet's number and address at the top, plus your number and a friend's backup. It'll make her feel much more confident.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I / leave her some money in case?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's thoughtful. A small amount in an envelope for a taxi to the vet or extra food would put both your minds at rest.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We're thinking of getting backyard chickens. Is it a lot of work?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A bit, but less than a dog. They need feeding and water every day, eggs collecting, and a coop clean once a week or so.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do they need a lot of space?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A few chickens are happy in a medium garden, as long as the coop is secure and they get time to scratch around.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about foxes?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's the big one. The coop needs to be fox proof, with a solid lock and wire buried under the run.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And noise?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hens are fairly quiet, just a bit of clucking. Roosters are the loud ones, and you don't need one to get eggs.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Huh, news to me.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A lot of people don't. Start with three hens, chickens are social and shouldn't live alone.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My husky is shedding so much the house looks like it snowed.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Huskies blow their coat twice a year, it's a lot. Brushing every day during these weeks really helps.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Every day? I barely brush my own hair.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ha, I get it. A good undercoat rake gets most of it out in ten minutes or so.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I shave him for summer?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Please don't. That double coat actually helps keep him cool, and it might not grow back properly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fine. / So just suffer?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Brush outside, vacuum often, and put a washable throw on his favourite spot. It passes in a few weeks.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Our hamster escaped last night. The cage door was open. Help.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Don't worry, they're usually still in the house. Close doors to keep him in one area and check behind sofas and under the fridge.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've looked everywhere.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hamsters come out at night. Put small piles of food in a few rooms and see which one gets eaten.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's clever.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You can also put a bit of flour around the food, so you'll see little footprints showing where he's going.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And then how do I catch him?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Put a deep bucket with some bedding and a treat at the bottom, with a ramp up to it. He'll climb in and can't get back out.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My cat keeps leaving dead mice on the doormat. Is she trying to tell me something?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: In a way. It's natural hunting behaviour, and some think cats bring prey home to the place they feel safe, or to share with their family.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It's very disgusting sharing.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ha, I understand. Don't tell her off, she won't connect it with the mouse.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I stop her hunting?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A bright collar with a quick release clasp can warn birds and mice. Keeping her in at dawn and dusk also cuts down on hunting.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And playing with her more?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, that helps a lot. Hunting style play with a wand toy, ending with a treat, can satisfy that instinct before she goes out.

option_sets.lead_in: We're finally getting a dog and we're choosing between a few at the shelter.
options: The first one is a young lab mix, super energetic, who needs a lot of walks and space.
Then there's an older beagle, calm and sweet, but he howls when he's left alone.
Option three is a small terrier mix that's great with kids but not with cats.
And the last one is a big shy greyhound who mostly wants to nap on the couch.
moshi_comment: It really depends on your home. The lab mix is great if you're active and have space, but needs a lot of time. The greyhound sounds surprisingly easy, since they're often happy to nap all day. The beagle's howling could be a problem if you're out at work.
Do you have a cat, and how long are you out of the house each day? If you have a cat, skip the terrier. If you're out a lot, the greyhound is probably the best fit.

option_sets.lead_in: My cat keeps scratching the furniture and I'm trying to pick a fix.
options: One option is a really tall scratching post right next to the couch.
Another is putting sticky tape on the arms of the sofa so she hates touching it.
Or I could get those soft caps that go over her claws, which last about a month.
moshi_comment: The tall scratching post is the best long term fix, since it gives her a place she's allowed to scratch. The sticky tape works well alongside it to steer her away from the couch. The soft caps work, but you'd have to keep putting them back on.
Have you tried a scratching post before? If not, I'd start with the tall post plus the tape for a few weeks. If she ignores the post completely, the claw caps are a good backup.

option_sets.lead_in: I'm working in the office three days a week again, and I need to sort out my dog during the day.
options: There's a doggy daycare near work, he'd play with other dogs all day, but it's pricey and he can be shy.
A dog walker could come at lunch for an hour, much cheaper, but he'd be home alone the rest of the time.
Or my retired neighbour offered to have him at her place, free, though she's not that strong on a lead.
moshi_comment: If he's shy, a whole day at daycare might be a lot for him at first. The lunchtime walker is a good middle ground if he's okay napping alone. The neighbour is lovely and free, but a strong puller and a not so strong walker is a worry.

How does he cope alone at the moment? If he's calm, the walker is the easy, affordable pick. If he gets anxious, the neighbour's company might suit him, as long as she just lets him snooze in the garden rather than walking him.

option_sets.lead_in: I live in a small flat and work long hours, but I'd really love some kind of pet.
options: I keep coming back to a cat, independent and cuddly, but my landlord would need to agree.
A pair of budgies would be cheerful and fit in a corner, though they can be pretty noisy.
There's also a fish tank, very calm and nice to look at, but you can't exactly cuddle a fish.
Or I could skip owning and volunteer walking dogs at the shelter on weekends.
moshi_comment: With long hours, the cat fits your life best, as long as the landlord agrees, cats cope well with being alone in the day. Budgies need more attention than people think. Fish are low effort if you want something calm.
If what you want is cuddles, the cat or the shelter walks are your real options. The volunteering is a great way to start without the commitment, and it'll show you how much time you really have.

option_sets.lead_in: Our kitten is about to graduate to a proper litter tray and I can't pick a litter.
options: The clumping clay one is cheap and easy to scoop, but it's dusty and gets tracked everywhere.
Pine pellets smell nice and are biodegradable, though some cats hate the feel under their paws.
And silica crystals soak up smells really well, but they're expensive and crunchy.
moshi_comment: Kittens are often fine with clumping clay since it feels like sand. The pine pellets are nice for the planet, but try a small bag first in case she refuses it. Crystals are great at smells, just pricey for a messy kitten.
I'd start her on a low dust clumping litter, it's the closest to what most cats like naturally. If you want to switch to pine later, mix it in slowly over a couple of weeks.

option_sets.lead_in: My dog chews the door frame when I'm at work, and I'm trying a few ideas.
options: One idea is a puzzle feeder and a frozen stuffed toy, so he has a job while I'm gone.
Another is a camera with a treat dispenser, I could talk to him and toss treats from my phone.
My sister thinks I should get a second dog to keep him company, which feels like a big leap.
Or I could book a trainer to come and look at whether it's boredom or anxiety.
moshi_comment: The trainer is the smartest first step, because boredom and anxiety need different fixes. The puzzle feeder is cheap and helps either way. I'd hold off on a second dog, it doesn't always calm the first one down.
Start with the puzzle feeder and a long walk before you leave. If the chewing continues, the camera will show you whether he's restless or stressed, and a trainer can take it from there.
